def process(waterBody2020, waterBody2021, waterBody2022, waterBody2023):
    import pandas as pd

    def prep(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        out = df[['Year', 'Beach Name', 'Beach Type Description', 'Violation']].copy()
        out['Violation'] = (
            out['Violation']
            .astype(str)
            .str.strip()
            .str.upper()
            .map({'YES': 1, 'NO': 0})
        )
        # keep only rows where we can interpret Violation as binary
        out = out[out['Violation'].isin([0, 1])]
        return out

    d2020, d2021, d2022, d2023 = map(prep, [waterBody2020, waterBody2021, waterBody2022, waterBody2023])

    # Only Fresh beaches
    d2020 = d2020[d2020['Beach Type Description'] == 'Fresh']
    d2021 = d2021[d2021['Beach Type Description'] == 'Fresh']
    d2022 = d2022[d2022['Beach Type Description'] == 'Fresh']
    d2023 = d2023[d2023['Beach Type Description'] == 'Fresh']

    # Beaches measured in all years (intersection of names)
    common = set(d2020['Beach Name']).intersection(d2021['Beach Name'], d2022['Beach Name'], d2023['Beach Name'])

    all_years = pd.concat([d2020, d2021, d2022, d2023], ignore_index=True)
    all_years = all_years[all_years['Beach Name'].isin(common)]

    # Exceedance rate = mean(Violation) across all samples since 2020
    rates = (
        all_years.groupby('Beach Name', as_index=False)['Violation']
        .mean()
        .rename(columns={'Violation': 'avgExceedanceRate'})
    )

    # Pick the max (tie-breaker: alphabetical)
    rates = rates.sort_values(['avgExceedanceRate', 'Beach Name'], ascending=[False, True]).reset_index(drop=True)
    return rates.head(1)

Concatenate all years and compute exceedance rate as mean(Violation) per Beach Name across all samples since 2020. Sort by avgExceedanceRate desc, then Beach Name asc (tie-break), return top 1 row with [Beach Name, avgExceedanceRate].
